name: World Liberty Financial
summary: A cryptocurrency company launched in 2024 by Trump family members with the Witkoff family and crypto entrepreneurs Zak Folkman and Chase Herro. It sells the WLFI governance token and issues the USD1 dollar stablecoin, and a Trump family entity takes 75% of token-sale revenue; Trump reported almost $800 million from it for 2025. A 49% stake sold for $500 million to a vehicle of the UAE national security adviser Sheikh Tahnoon days before Trump’s inauguration, and the use of USD1 for an Abu Dhabi fund’s $2 billion Binance investment, have drawn conflict-of-interest scrutiny.

connections.name: Donald Trump
connections.description: Introduced as its “chief crypto advocate” at the 2024 launch and listed as co-founder emeritus since taking office. His family’s DT Marks DEFI LLC is its largest owning entity on the Trump side and a Trump entity takes 75% of token-sale revenue; his 2025 financial disclosure reported almost $800 million from World Liberty. Trump said his sons run it.

connections.name: Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan
connections.description: UAE national security adviser. His vehicle Aryam Investment 1 agreed in January 2025, days before Trump’s inauguration, to buy 49% of the company for $500 million, per the Wall Street Journal; of the first $250 million, $187 million went to Trump family entities and about $31 million to Witkoff-linked firms, and Aryam and G42 got two board seats. A company spokesman confirmed the stake; Trump said he did not know of it.

The figures are from different dates.

source_conflicts.topic: Whether Steve Witkoff left the company
source_conflicts.details: The White House counsel said Witkoff had divested from World Liberty; Sen. Adam Schiff and seven colleagues wrote in October 2025 that his August 2025 disclosure showed he still held his crypto assets, and Bloomberg-based reports said he had not yet sold his World Liberty stake.

notes: Researched with web searches; the Wall Street Journal’s February 2026 report on the Aryam stake and several Reuters investigations are cited through outlets that reported on them. Not in the links: token sales of about $550 million by March 2025 (Bloomberg); an OCC preliminary conditional approval on August 14, 2026 for World Liberty Trust Company, a national trust bank to issue USD1 (Crowdfund Insider; application per The Block); a WLFI buyback announced in November 2026 after the token fell more than 60% in 2026 (Reuters via Investing.com); and House Democrats’ plans to investigate it when they take control of the Oversight Committee in 2027 (crypto.news, Bankless). A January 2026 memorandum with Pakistan’s finance ministry on using USD1 for cross-border payments was non-binding (Al Jazeera).
